what: A mirror of the registry baseline's own deliberate departures from the literature, row for row and word for word. The lab prints it ahead of every scenario's own departures, so 'no departures' is never read as 'the literature'. Not edited by hand: regenerate from the source.

source.status: MIRROR OF AN UNMERGED PULL REQUEST. Re-pin `reference` and `commit` to the merge commit when stapledons-design #64 lands (the scenario files name the same reference, so their digests change then), and move the check to lore-import.

departures.size: The prior's mean falls from 5.43 × 10⁸ to 7.24 × 10⁶ yr (LW-46): 1.88 dex
departures.reason: A civilisation that outlasts the 5 Gyr window (LW-11) never ends in play, and the count formula alive = everTech × L / window stops being a share once L nears the window. Ruled: D-144; kept as OQ2 of R3-UNIVERSE-LAB (D-156)

departures.literature: 10⁶ yr, the median of Sandberg's range
departures.reason: It follows from row 1: the median of a log-uniform range is the geometric middle of its ends

departures.baseline: fLife is the chance that a habitable-zone world has a biosphere
departures.literature: Sandberg §3.1.1: a rate model for "evolutionarily competent life"
departures.size: None on the number; it changes what the number means
departures.reason: The game needs a state a telescope can read (a biosphere), not a rate

departures.baseline: fTech is "builds technology"; L is the technological lifetime
departures.literature: Sandberg §1: f_c is "detectable/contactable"; L is the longevity "of such detectable civilizations"
departures.size: None, if §6 is obeyed. A second "detectable" share would count it twice (the old one in ten: 1 dex)
departures.reason: The game models detection with instruments, so "detectable" must not be a hidden extra factor

departures.baseline: Stars and planets come from measurements: density LW-1, occurrence LW-52 = 0.20 habitable-zone worlds per star
departures.literature: Sandberg Table 1: R★, f_p and n_e are log-uniform (1–100 per year; 0.1–1; 0.1–1). The medians give f_p × n_e = 0.10
departures.reason: The map is made of real stars. The count is over space near the Sun, not a Galactic birth rate

departures.baseline: M-dwarf habitable zones count in full: 0.12 of the 0.20 (LW-4 × LW-6)
departures.literature: Disputed. Snyder-Beattie et al. 2021 predict M-dwarf planets are uninhabitable; Shields et al. 2016 review the open questions (both read at the abstract only, in seti-factors §3.6–§3.7)
departures.size: 0.40 dex fewer worlds if they are excluded
departures.reason: Ruled: life feature decision 3. Each such world is labelled "habitability debated"

departures.baseline: Onsets are uniform over 5 Gyr centred on now; planets have no ages (LW-11)
departures.literature: Star formation is not flat (Mor et al. 2019); most Earth-like planets are older than Earth (Lineweaver 2001). Both read at the abstract only
departures.size: About ±0.5 dex, sign unknown: an estimate, not a calculation
departures.reason: One keyed draw per world gives the same history in every preset. A planet-age model is a named follow-up (R3-UNIVERSE-LAB UL-E)

departures.baseline: One technological lineage per planet, ever
departures.literature: No source measures this. Wright 2018 and Schmidt & Frank 2019 treat an earlier species as an open question
departures.size: None at the prior medians (a second lineage is a 10⁻⁵ event). It caps the dial at 2.70 dex in the fractions
departures.reason: The exact propagation law assumes one lineage. Successive lineages are ruled in as a later option (seti-factors §5.8, ruling 2)

departures.baseline: Every civilisation in one universe has the same lifetime L
departures.literature: Lifetimes are a population; what is detected is length-biased (Kipping, Frank & Scharf 2020, abstract only)
departures.size: None on counts at equal mean; it changes who is met
departures.reason: The dial sets one L. A spread is a named follow-up (UL-B)

departures.literature: Hart 1975, Newman & Sagan 1981, Carroll-Nellenback et al. 2019: a long-lived civilisation spreads (seti-factors §3.3)
departures.size: −0.6 to −1.0 dex of luck needed, if 3 to 9 daughter worlds each
departures.reason: Ruled out of the default (seti-factors §5.8, ruling 4)

departures.baseline: Ending shares 0.75 / 0.15 / 0.10 (LW-34 to LW-36); remnant traces last 10³ to 10⁷ yr (LW-37, LW-38); the complex-life split (LW-12)
departures.literature: No source gives any of these
departures.reason: The game needs ended states and ruins. D-144

departures.literature: The same paper's corrected density is 0.081 ± 0.003
departures.reason: Kept from the approved reference; inside the paper's error

departures.baseline: A local thin disc only: no radial gradient, no thick disc or halo (LW-2)
departures.literature: Jurić et al. 2008 fit two discs and a halo
departures.size: Small inside 3000 ly; not valid toward the Galactic centre
departures.reason: The play area is local. The pilgrim to Sgr A* waits for the model galaxy

departures.literature: Reylé et al. 2021 count objects within 10 pc; the 0.75 is not a measured share for this model's denominator
departures.reason: Kept as the approved nominal value
